0xf3cd/bazi.body:
# Bazi

A Python 3.11+ Bazi chart library for Chinese-speaking users, providing Four Pillars, Five Elements, Ten Gods, Nayin, relationships, and luck-cycle (流运) queries.
It can also be used without creating a chart, directly consulting knowledge entries that come with sources and stated limits of applicability. At runtime it uses only the standard library and bundled data, and makes no network connections.

## Installation

Install into an existing Python, conda, or virtual environment:

```sh
python -m pip install bazi
```

To create a new environment, choose a version on the [documentation site](https://0xf3cd.github.io/bazi/) and read "Quick Start". Ordinary use does not require testing or documentation build tools.

## Create the First Chart

The example below uses fictional birth information, entered in the Gregorian calendar on UTC+8 (East Eight Zone) clock time; the default entry point does not convert time zones automatically.
You can run it directly in the Python interactive environment, or save it as a UTF-8 script and run it; do not name the script `bazi.py`, so it does not shadow the installed package.

```python
from bazi.bazi import 八字
from bazi.bazi_chart import 命盘

盘 = 命盘(八字.create('1990-05-17 10:30', '女'))
print('四柱', ' '.join(map(str, 盘.八字.四柱)))
print('日主', 盘.八字.日主)
print('年干十神', 盘.十神.年.天干)
```

```text
四柱 庚午 辛巳 壬午 乙巳
日主 壬
年干十神 偏印
```

The four pillars are in order: year, month, day, hour. Gender accepts `女`／`男` or `female`／`male`.
Chinese names and original names such as `Bazi` and `BaziChart` may be mixed; import types from their defining modules.
The default is `DAY` precision and a day-pillar change at 23:00. `DAY` compares solar terms by date only, but the birth hour is still used for the hour pillar.
For methods of entering overseas local clock time and true solar time, see the "Configuration and Time Conventions" section for the corresponding version on the [documentation site](https://0xf3cd.github.io/bazi/).

## Continued Use

Choose a released version to read on the [documentation site](https://0xf3cd.github.io/bazi/); documentation for the current source code is also available in the [development documentation](https://0xf3cd.github.io/bazi/dev/).

"Quick Start" covers chart text, saving results, and optional environment setup; other guides include "Configuration and Time Conventions", "Gregorian, Lunar Calendars and Solar Terms", "Relationships and Luck Cycles", "Integrated Development", and "Consulting the Knowledge Base"; the knowledge catalog and API reference are available for reference at any time.

When you only need Gregorian–lunar conversion, import `to_lunar` and `to_date` from `bazi.calendar.utils`; there is no need to create a chart.
For round-trip examples and leap-month numbering, see the "Gregorian, Lunar Calendars and Solar Terms" guide for the selected version on the [documentation site](https://0xf3cd.github.io/bazi/).

Ahoo-Wang/CoSec.body:
# CoSec

Multi-tenant, non-blocking authorization for Spring: IAM-style policy documents and role-based permissions,
evaluated deny-first for every request.

> [Documentation](https://cosec.ahoo.me/) | [中文文档](https://cosec.ahoo.me/zh/)

## Why CoSec

- **Policies as data.** Platform, app and tenant documents in JSON: statements on actions and resources, typed
  conditions (roles, tenant, app and space, IP ranges, time windows, external attributes), and bindings that say
  who each policy applies to. Every instance compiles them into a snapshot read from Redis and picks up published
  changes without a restart.
- **Deny wins, everywhere.** Any matching DENY overrides every ALLOW, in any document; unmatched requests are
  denied; a request that cannot be decided fails closed with `503`, with two documented exceptions: while the revocation store cannot be read a request's token is accepted unless `cosec.authentication.revocation.fail-closed` is `true`, and past the bounded snapshot lag only the tenants in `cosec.authorization.snapshot.fail-closed.tenants` answer `503` ([Security model](https://cosec.ahoo.me/guide/security-model#the-two-documented-exceptions)).

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

LeXwDeX/GraphAgent.body:
# GraphAgent

> A terminal coding agent that runs dynamic workflows: the main agent designs the dependency graph itself, sub-agents execute in parallel waves, state is persisted, and it can recover after a crash.

GraphAgent is a standalone terminal coding agent focused on dynamic DAG workflows. It originated from an early version of opencode and has been maintained independently since v2.0.

A single agent loop handles one-shot tasks without problems. Once a task has ordering dependencies, parts that can run in parallel, or needs a review midway, it struggles: work that should run in parallel runs serially, and intermediate conclusions go unreviewed. If the process crashes, you have to start over from scratch. GraphAgent lets the main agent first draw the task as a dependency graph, then execute according to that graph. The graph is not predefined; it is designed on the fly for the task, so DAG workflows are essentially dynamic workflows.

Each node in the graph is a real sub-session with its own agent and context window. Nodes whose dependencies are all satisfied form a wave and run in parallel within that wave. State is persisted as events, so it can be paused, stepped through, and replanned. After a crash, it recovers from the persisted record without replaying model calls from scratch.

## Project status

v2.0 is under development and about to be released. Release progress is tracked in the [milestone](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/milestone/7). For reproducible problems, please open an [Issue](https://github.com/LeXwDeX/GraphAgent/issues).

# UnipusAI-Helper

A course-completion tool for the U-Campus AI edition, built on Selenium, PySide6 / QML, and OpenAI-compatible APIs

## FAQ

> Answers to a few common questions 🤔

**Doesn't feel very easy to use**

U-Campus covers a lot of textbooks, and support for different courses and question types is still being improved. The project also has plenty of room to grow. If you run into problems, please report them in an issue, and if you're able, PRs are welcome.

**Why use Selenium browser automation instead of calling the API directly to report completion?**

Reporting progress directly is faster, but the platform may have detection mechanisms, and that approach carries higher risk, not only to your account but also legal risk. chen1111-a/hkid-quota-monitor.body:
# Hong Kong ID Card Booking Quota Dashboard

Monitors smart ID card booking quotas at the six Hong Kong Immigration Department Personal Registration Offices, checking about every 2 minutes, and notifies subscribers via email / Feishu group when slots are released. **A third-party public-benefit tool, not an official service of the Immigration Department. It only monitors and sends reminders, and does not grab or book on anyone's behalf.**

## Dashboard entry

- **Preferred (stable direct access from mainland China)**: https://hkid-quota-monitor.pages.dev/
- Backup: https://chen1111-a.github.io/hkid-quota-monitor/
  (From mainland networks, github.io is intermittently unreachable. jsDelivr/raw direct links carry a nosniff header and only display source code, so do not use them as web entry points.)
- The full experience in mainland China without a VPN is through **email subscription + Feishu group**. The notification path is entirely direct within China and pushes to your phone the moment slots are released. The dashboard is only a helper.

## How it works

```
cron-job.org (every 2 minutes) ──▶ GitHub Actions
                            │  python -m quota_monitor.run
                            │  ├─ fetch Immigration Department public quota API (read-only, one request per run)
                            │  ├─ diff against previous snapshot → slot-release events
                            │  └─ commit data/ + refresh jsDelivr cache
                            ▼
        index.html dashboard (mobile-first, auto-refreshes every 90 seconds)
        Email + Feishu notifications (triggered by slot-release events, with debounce cooldown)
```

- API structure: [docs/api-notes.md](https://github.com/chen1111-a/hkid-quota-monitor/blob/HEAD/docs/api-notes.md)
- 2-minute trigger configuration: [docs/cron-setup.md](https://github.com/chen1111-a/hkid-quota-monitor/blob/HEAD/docs/cron-setup.md)

## Improvements over similar tools

- **Mobile-first**: dates scroll vertically in rows, all 6 offices fit on one screen, no horizontal table scrolling
- **Colorblind-friendly**: status cells use both color and text (available / low / full)
- **Anti-notification-flooding**: the official API has load-balancing data jitter (observed 304↔346 cell fluctuation within the same minute), so the notification layer has a per-cell cooldown and won't alert on every cycle
- **Direct access in mainland China**: email subscription and Feishu notification paths are directly reachable within China, no VPN needed
- Light and dark themes; summary cards directly show the earliest date you can book

# Polaris

Polaris is an AI Agent governance and runtime platform for complex software delivery scenarios.  
Its goal is not to build yet another Agent shell that "chats and calls tools," but to turn Agent execution into an engineering system that is **transactional, auditable, rollback-capable, and verifiable**.

The English version of this README is at [README.en.md](https://github.com/dainsiahtill-dev/Polaris/blob/HEAD/README.en.md).

Architecturally:

- `KernelOne` is the underlying runtime foundation, responsible for general capabilities such as context, execution, side effects, storage layout, and events
- `Cells` are business capability boundaries, breaking complex systems into governable capability units
- New engineering runs are handled by `EngineeringRunService` and a single per-project SQLite record; ContextOS provides final request observation. `TransactionKernel` belongs to the historical execution chain.

## Project Overview

Polaris is an AI Agent governance and runtime platform for complex software delivery scenarios.  
It is not trying to solve "can the model call a few more tools." It addresses more fundamental questions:

- How a single Agent execution can have clear boundaries
- How context can be upgraded from accumulated messages into a runtime system
- How tool calls and state modifications can enter an auditable chain
- How multi-role, multi-stage, long-running tasks can form verifiable closed loops

Polaris can be understood as two layers:

1. `KernelOne`
   The underlying runtime foundation for AI Agents, responsible for platform-independent capabilities such as context, execution, side effects, storage layout, events, and runtime contracts.
2. `Polaris`
   A governance and delivery system built on `KernelOne`, responsible for multi-role collaboration, task orchestration, execution scheduling, audit and acceptance, quality gates, and the desktop workbench.

In other words, Polaris is closer to an **Agent Runtime + Governance Platform** than to a collection of prompt templates or a chat-style coding assistant.

# Thunder Pelican · 雷霆鹈鹕

> A pelican with lightning in its eye rides a bicycle through the storm coast.

`Canvas 2D` · `No dependencies` · `No build step` · `GitHub Pages ready`



[Release notes for this update](https://github.com/imnotorangewong/Thunder-Pelican/blob/HEAD/更新说明.md)

## Project Overview

The main game is in `index.html`: the classic pelican, bicycle, coast, lightning, and UI are all drawn with Canvas. There are also 12 original rider skins and 13 rider forms, with transparent WebP illustrations loaded on demand. The Day & Night Twin Dragons is a skin that can switch between dark and light forms. Each character's themed emblem should stay on the character itself, keeping the shape and proportions of the reference image. It should be clearly recognizable but not enlarged to overshadow the main subject, and must not be stretched or distorted.

A few design choices that are a bit meticulous:

- The bicycle and pelican are hand-drawn. When the pedal turns one revolution, the legs move one revolution too; road bumps carry through to the frame.
- The second gear of Thunder is not just a speed boost: first the dragon lifts its head, then it lowers itself on landing, and sits upright again when it ends.
- The wheels throw lightning. Lightning arcs branch randomly, last less than a fraction of a second, and the ground-contact impact has a shock flash.
- Scores have no cap. Combo, no-damage, and overclock form three independent multiplier zones that widen the gap between players.
- After the second gear of Thunder is activated, it measures peak Space presses over three seconds. At least 3 CPS is needed to boost; the current second-gear cap is 198 KM/H.
- There is only one leaderboard, on the server. Open it with the "Leaderboard" button in the top bar. `One best score per person`; it is overwritten only when a new record is set.
- After a score is uploaded, the server re-verifies it with the same formula; altered scores cannot enter the leaderboard. If the connection fails, the score is queued and resubmitted next time you're online.
- Local riders can still be ranked by total score, single-run score, speed, and number of skins. That ranks who is on this machine, not a competitive leaderboard.
- Each run issues a contract: maintain speed, lightning chains, no damage, and so on. Complete it to earn points, then move on to the next one.
- A glowing whale occasionally drifts across the sky. Tap it three times and it will drop something.
- Eighteen skins in total: the classic pelican, 12 original riders (13 character forms in total, with the Day & Night Twin Dragons switchable), and 5 hidden event characters.
- Badge numbers, titles, and progress are only written to this machine's localStorage. No registration is required, and nothing is uploaded.
- As soon as the page opens, the theme song loops. Sound is split into three channels, **background music / game sound effects / skin voices**, each with its own toggle and volume.
- Click "Timed Challenge" to start a run, then click "End Challenge" to end early and keep the fastest time for that run. It settles automatically after 30 seconds.
- When a run ends, a settlement panel appears with: final score, fastest time in this run, all-time fastest time, global ranking, and an A–E overall grade.

The "Creators Say" panel in the top right shows the GitHub avatars, credits, school emblems, and shared message of the two creators. Click an avatar to open that creator's GitHub profile.

The riding screen permanently displays speed, journey score, and bottom action controls. Click "Current Contract" to view tasks and progress. Skin unlock notifications appear from the top right, and riding continues uninterrupted.

# dsh-studio

A "requirements & task workspace" for internal company use: a resident DSH plugin that packs **kanban board + role agents + internal marketplace** into the same page of DSH Web.
Source code is managed on a self-hosted GitLab and communication runs through Feishu. Agents handle the concrete work of four roles: product / architecture / development / testing.

Runtime environment: DSH `0.2.2-rc.1`, Node 22 or above, Linux/macOS (native Windows is not supported for `link:` installation + systemd hosting).

Maintenance: Supply Chain Digitalization team. For questions, open an issue in this repository or contact the "product" role on the board directly. For the release process, see [docs/publish.md](https://github.com/marsken88/dsh-studio/blob/HEAD/docs/publish.md).

## Feature map

Organized in the order of "a requirement from birth to end-of-life". For details, see the topic docs; the implementation log is in [docs/history.md](https://github.com/marsken88/dsh-studio/blob/HEAD/docs/history.md).

| Stage | Capability |
| --- | --- |
| Requirements | Unified numbering, feature breakdown, traceability matrix, open-questions list, RICE requirement pool, change history |
| Clarification | Mandatory answers and a gate before cards are split (`src/host/discovery.js`); work cannot start if answers are incomplete |
| Design | Design review records and a gate before development begins (`src/host/design.js`) |
| Execution | One card per session, one card per worktree; automatic dispatch to the four expert types: product, architecture, development, and testing |
| Test cases | Three executors: API, shell, and database; **test cases with reliable assertions are trial-run immediately after being written**; cross-card test case overview (can show only the ones without assertions); failures automatically open defect cards |
| Exit criteria | Two-level exit at card and requirement levels, acceptance checklist, coverage matrix, manual sign-off |
| Release | Version tags, canary and deployment records, smoke checklist, release gate |
| Observability | Workbench (in progress / overdue / blocked / defects), efficiency metrics (cycle-time distribution / rework / AI cost), burndown |

# Songloft Player (Lynx)

The Lynx client for Songloft Player, completely rewritten from the Flutter version to ReactLynx + TypeScript. Supports four platforms: Android / iOS / HarmonyOS / Web.

To learn about the underlying technology: [Lynx official website](https://lynxjs.org/) · [ReactLynx official documentation](https://lynxjs.org/react/).

"Settings → Playback settings → Keep screen on on the lyrics page" is off by default and is stored only on the local device. When enabled, the screen stays on while lyrics are visible (in wide-screen mode, lyrics are shown side by side). This still applies while playback is paused. Returning to the cover, leaving the player, or switching to the background restores automatic screen-off. Android/iOS/HarmonyOS require a native installation package that includes the new screen-on API; older shells degrade safely. On Web, this depends on browser Screen Wake Lock support and permissions; if the request is denied, playback is not affected.

## Current status

The project is currently positioned as a **preview release**. Core playback, library/playlists, lyrics, plugins, themes, multi-server support, and management settings are already implemented. The About page now separately provides client update checks and server update checks: dev checks only dev, and stable releases check only the latest stable release. Native bundle updaters for all three platforms are integrated into the source code. On Android, local interface download/cancel/cold-start verification is complete; iOS/HarmonyOS build and device acceptance remain open. The signing key for official updates has not yet been configured. Old shells or incompatible updates provide an installer entry point for this channel. See the [client update protocol](https://github.com/songloft-org/songloft-player-lynx/blob/HEAD/docs/reference/client-updates.md) for details. Windows/macOS desktop hosts, Bundle, playback, both plugin types, and full application updates have a [candidate implementation](https://github.com/songloft-org/songloft-player-lynx/blob/HEAD/desktop/README.md). As requested, implementation is completed first, with unified acceptance at the end. The current device matrix and official distribution remain open. See the [implementation record](https://github.com/songloft-org/songloft-player-lynx/blob/HEAD/docs/project/desktop-implementation.md) for details.

# claude-rotator

An unofficial proxy tool that automatically switches between multiple Claude Code accounts locally, depending on the request's model and usage quota. Works on macOS and Linux.

`claude-rotator` starts an Anthropic-compatible HTTP proxy that listens only on `127.0.0.1`, and points `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` in Claude Code's `~/.claude/settings.json` to this proxy. After installation, Claude Code can still be launched as usual with the `claude` command.

**Zero dependencies** ([package.json](https://github.com/taskbrain/claude-rotator/blob/HEAD/package.json) has no `dependencies`; it is implemented using only the Node.js standard library). Because there is no supply chain risk from external packages, the cost of auditing the code by reading it is kept low.

It is not distributed through the npm registry (`package.json` has `"private": true`). To use it, clone this repository and install it locally with `npm install -g .`.

yuan-SiO2/ComfyUI-Yuan-Tool.body:
# ComfyUI-Yuan-Tool

A collection of ComfyUI custom nodes for **timeline workflows** targeting MiniMax H3 video generation. It includes nodes for images, text, audio, CLIP timelines, and guidance injection.

## Installation

```bash
cd ComfyUI/custom_nodes
git clone https://github.com/yuan-SiO2/ComfyUI-Yuan-Tool.git
```

Dependencies (`requirements.txt`): `opencv-python`, `numpy`, `Pillow`, `color-matcher`, `nvidia-vfx`, `av`, `torchaudio`, `scenedetect` (torch is provided by ComfyUI). The "Yuan Video Save" node also requires FFmpeg. It is provided by `imageio-ffmpeg` by default, or you can use a system `ffmpeg` or the environment variable `YUAN_FFMPEG_PATH`.

## Node List

### Image (Yuan Tool/图像)

| Node | Description |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Multi-frame Reference** | Expands a subject image or background image into a reference frame sequence with time-aware attention. Outputs one 64×64 blank image as a fallback when there are no valid inputs. |
| **Filter Images** | Filters an image list by frame count and start frame. Out-of-range indices are automatically cropped. Outputs a blank image as a fallback when there are no valid inputs. |
| **Load Batch Images** | Batch image loader with up to 20 tracks. Uses center crop to prevent distortion. Sizes are aligned to multiples of 16. |
| **Image Point Processing** | Embedded canvas with point annotations (left-click for positive, right-click for negative) and box annotations (drag/resize). Supports frame-by-frame annotation across multiple frames. Outputs coordinate JSON, bounding boxes, and frame indices. |
| **Image Grid Stitch** | Arranges batch images into a grid of width × height at equal intervals. With few images, they are spread evenly, with empty cells filled black. With many images, they are sampled at equal intervals, always keeping the first and last. All images are scaled to the size of the first image. Saves to the output directory using "filename prefix + number". The prefix may include subdirectories. The number directly determines the `_00001_` segment, and repeated runs overwrite files. |
| **Load Output Image** | Reads images from the output directory using "filename prefix + number" (same rule as Save Image: `{prefix}_{number:05}_.png`). Outputs the image and mask. Outputs a blank image if the file does not exist. |

yuyukj888/shcap.body:
# SHCAP

**The continuation of NapCat · A modernized OneBot 11 protocol endpoint for QQ bots**

[Quick Start](#一快速开始) · [Email Alerts](#四邮件告警) · [FAQ](#六常见问题) · [Contact & Sponsorship](#八联系与赞助)

---

## What is this

SHCAP is a continuation of [NapCat](https://github.com/NapNeko/NapCatQQ) (independently maintained, based on NapCat 4.18.42). It turns 'QQ bot + OneBot 11' into a finished product that **works right after installation**:

- Compatible with **OneBot 11**: supports HTTP / WebSocket forward (server) and reverse (client) modes
- Keeps the **NapCat plugin ecosystem**: `.napcat-plugin` and `plugins/` directories work out of the box
- Built-in **WebUI**: token login, real-time logs, online config editing, plugin management, version management
- Built-in **HTML email alerts**: disconnects, recoveries, login failures, and verification requests all send emails that are easy to read on both phones and computers
- **Fast login without re-verification after restart**: fixed hostname + graceful shutdown, so rebuilding a container no longer repeatedly requires new device verification
- Independent branding and a blue theme (SH identity), no longer dependent on the upstream repository

> **About the QQ version**: the image contains QQ **3.2.35**. NapCat 4.18.42's offset table mainly covers the 3.2.30–3.2.35 range.
> If you replace the QQ deb package yourself, make sure `main` in `/opt/QQ/resources/app/package.json` is set back to `./loadNapCat.js`.
> Otherwise only the QQ process runs, with no NapCat (see [Packaging your own QQ version](#打包自己的-qq-版本)).

---

## I. Quick Start

The official image `ghcr.io/yuyukj888/shcap` already includes the **SHCAP interface, HTML email templates, and the graceful shutdown patch**.
**Pull it and you have SHCAP**. You don't need to download a Shell package or overwrite any files.

> The image is about 1.57 GB and includes its runtime dependencies (there is no node/npm inside the container).
> Current digest: `sha256:ca49a492028c7ed562bc217919dc5cb45fe53612c3ac820f85ca26de7a074d7c`
